finding.claim: wipe() calls requireRole(u, "OWNER") but discards its boolean return value, so the OWNER check is a no-op and any authenticated user can reach repo.wipe(tenant).
finding.source: POST /tenants/{t}/wipe (src/Admin.java:24-25) with any authenticated User; tenant comes from the path.

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) entry point; no other auth gate.
requireRole(u, "OWNER") called; return value ignored; requireRole returns boolean and never throws (line 13-16).

finding.guards_checked: requireRole (Admin.java:14-16) returns a boolean and does not throw; its result is unused at line 26. Sibling export() (Admin.java:31-34) uses checkRole (throws, lines 18-22) and is correctly enforced, showing the intended pattern. No tenant-ownership check exists in either handler; User record (line 4) has no tenant field, so cross-tenant scoping cannot be verified from this repo (uncertain, not reported as a separate finding).

verdict.guard_found: None effective. requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) returns a boolean and never throws, and wipe() calls it as a bare statement at line 26 with the result discarded. checkRole (lines 18-22) would throw, but wipe() does not call it. No other check exists between wipe() (line 25) and repo.wipe (line 27).
verdict.reason: Every line in the trace matches the code: src/Admin.java:26 calls requireRole and discards its boolean result, so src/Admin.java:27 runs for any User that reaches wipe(), and the sibling export() at lines 31-34 uses the throwing checkRole. The attacker is an authenticated low-privilege user; the repo does not show the router or whether tenant scoping applies, but that does not affect the role-check bypass itself.
